artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Waiata, released in 1981, is the sixth studio album by New Zealand new wave band Split Enz, issued internationally by A&M Records (and as Corroboree in Australia). The album continues the band's exploration of a polished new wave and rock sound, blending catchy pop melodies with art-rock sensibilities. It features contributions from key members Tim and Neil Finn, with production by David Tickle, and was recorded at AAV Studios in Melbourne. Musically, it balances energetic rhythms and melodic hooks with the quirky, theatrical style that had become a hallmark of Split Enz's work.

In the context of Split Enz's discography, Waiata followed the commercial breakthrough of True Colours (1980) and helped solidify the band's international presence. Although it did not surpass the massive success of its predecessor, Waiata achieved significant commercial acclaim, reaching number one on the album charts in both New Zealand and Australia and entering the U.S. Top 50. The album includes notable tracks like "History Never Repeats," which exemplify the band's blend of pop accessibility and new wave edge. Critical reception was mixed to positive, with some reviewers appreciating its polished production and songwriting, though it was sometimes seen as less groundbreaking than earlier releases.

Overall, Waiata represents a key moment in Split Enz's evolution from an art-rock ensemble to a more mainstream rock and pop act, maintaining their distinctive style while appealing to a broader audience. Its success helped pave the way for their subsequent album Time and Tide (1982), continuing their string of chart-topping releases in the early 1980s.
